newsitem.title: FRANCE: Three bombs explode on Corsica, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Three bombs explode on Corsica, no casualties.

text.p: Three bombs planted by suspected separatist guerrillas exploded on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica, causing damage but no casualties, police said on Thursday.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the bombs which went off late on Wednesday night in the ports of Bonifacio and Porto-Vecchio in the south and Bastia in the north.
Police said the attacks bore the hallmarks of guerrillas who have been waging a low-level bombing campaign for two decades for more autonomy from mainland France.

The bomb in Bonifacio blew out two doors and damaged the reception hall of the chamber of commerce and industry. The Porto-Vecchio bomb, planted in a France Telecom office, caused extensive damage. The third bomb exploded at a customs office in Bastia and also caused wide damage.
